takeaway: The left coronary artery divides into the anterior interventricular and circumflex arteries; the right coronary gives the posterior interventricular artery.

question.text: Concerning the blood supply and drainage of the heart, which statement is correct?

answer.text: The circumflex artery arises from the left coronary artery.

lines.text: Look at the picture: the aorta gives off the coronary arteries just above the aortic valve.
The left coronary artery arises from the aortic sinus, and soon divides in two.
One branch is the anterior interventricular artery, running down the front groove.
The other is the circumflex artery, curling round the atrioventricular groove. So the circumflex comes from the left coronary.
The right coronary artery is a separate vessel from the aorta.
It gives the posterior interventricular artery, which meets the anterior one in the groove.
So the anterior interventricular does not come from the right, and the circumflex arises from the left.
lines.say: (sigh) So the anterior interventricular does not come from the right, and the circumflex arises from the left.
